description: We are TRIAX, a team of three students: Ahmed, Amr, and Ezzat. We are interested in programming, AI, science, and space exploration. Our goal is to use technology and creativity to solve real-world problems. We enjoy teamwork, learning new skills, and turning ideas into useful projects. We are excited to take part in NASA Space Apps Challenge and create something meaningful.
summary: MOON BASE 360 is an interactive, browser-based mission trainer where young learners manage a lunar outpost, balance critical life-support resources, and make real engineering trade-offs. Powered by NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) science, the game bridges the gap between overly simplistic space trivia and complex orbital tools. By offering bilingual (English/Arabic) gameplay across the Lunar South Pole and Equatorial regions, MOON BASE 360 makes Artemis-era lunar exploration accessible, engaging, and rooted in systems-thinking decision-making.
details:
What It Does:

MOON BASE 360 puts students in the role of a lunar outpost crew commander. Players navigate a lunar rover across four key locations—the Main Base, a Sunlit Ridge, a Permanently Shadowed Crater, and a Research Lab—to complete four scientific discoveries per mission while keeping their crew alive.

How It Works:

1. Region & Difficulty Selection: Players choose between the South Pole (Ice Explorer) and the Equatorial Region (Sun Explorer), along with three difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Hard) and an instant English/Arabic language toggle.

2. Resource Trade-Offs: Every rover movement and exploration action consumes Oxygen and Energy. Players must monitor four live telemetry meters (Oxygen, Energy, Water, and Safety) and return to the base to recover resources.

3. Discovery & Quiz Loop: Each region contains 7 tailored discoveries (14 total) covering lunar power generation, polar water ice, thermal insulation, regolith radiation shielding, and closed-loop life support. Each discovery includes a science explanation and an interactive quiz question that boosts crew Safety when answered correctly.

Benefits & Future Roadmap:

Today, the prototype features a working 5-step gameplay loop, 14 NASA-grounded discoveries, live resource meters, a Discovery Journal, and bilingual support. Planned post-hackathon updates include dedicated Food Production and Radiation Exposure meters, dynamic solar-flare hazard events, a Mars outpost comparison mode, and an educator dashboard for classrooms.

Tools & Technologies Used:

Developed by Team AEE X (Ahmed Hossam, Ezzat Tamer, Amr Gamal) using HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript for zero-install, cross-device browser execution.
